answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence a shared reputation score. A nebula of fresh identities then gains no voting weight until it earns trust through costly, verifiable work; if accounts coordinate to submit fake results, auditors can challenge them and slash the stake. The attacker must therefore fund every identity and risk losing that capital, while a raven or umber-themed profile offers no shortcut.
